neighbours.label: the token right after a body-part noun in a phrase about what is done with that body part ('teeth [baring]', 'eyeball [rolling]', 'blood [vessels]', 'bones [in]')
fire: The meeting ended with a lot of hand wringing and very little agreement.
After the defeat there was plenty of finger pointing among the coaches.
The children ate their soup with loud lip smacking and giggles.
The dog welcomed us home with frantic tail wagging at the gate.
Her nerves showed in the constant nail biting during the interview.
The toddlers settled their argument with some hair pulling and tears.
It took a little arm twisting before he agreed to give the speech.
The crowd answered the announcement with foot stamping and whistles.
quiet: The meeting ended with a lot of paper shuffling and very little agreement.
After the defeat there was plenty of blame shifting among the coaches.
The children ate their soup with loud spoon clattering and giggles.
The town welcomed us home with cheerful flag waving at the gate.
Her nerves showed in the constant pen clicking during the interview.
The toddlers settled their argument with some toy throwing and tears.
It took a little horse trading before he agreed to give the speech.
The crowd answered the announcement with door slamming and whistles.

notes: Weak, mixed pole (max 9.4, no dominant token, several Korean/Russian examples). English top examples put the peak right after a body noun (blood vessels, bones in, eyeball rolling, teeth baring, intestines at, my body for); probes 0.2-0.49 on those and 0.10 on 'roads in'. The + pole fires on the action word before a body part (wagging, crossing your arms), so the two poles may split action / body part. Near misses keep the noun+gerund frame with a non-body noun. Low confidence.
